text.p: BankBoston Corp said Wednesday it will evaluate the results of an investigation into Mercury Finance Co's accounting before proceeding with a proposed deal to sell its consumer finance unit to Mercury.

"We were surprised and disappointed to learn today of the discovery of accounting irregularities at Mercury Finance Company," BankBoston said. "We will carefully evaluate the results of the ongoing investigation being conducted by the special committee of Mercury's Board before proceeding with the pending transaction involving Fidelity Acceptance Corporation."

On Jan. 10, Mercury announced its agreement to issue 32.7 million common shares, or about 16 percent of its total outstanding shares, to BankBoston in exchange for Fidelity Acceptance Corp. The value of the transaction was placed at $392.5 million on Jan. 10.

Mercury said earlier it discovered accounting irregularities which caused an overstatement of its earnings over the past four years. The accounting irregularities appear to be the result of unauthorized entries being made to the accounting records of the company by its principal accounting officer, who has disappeared and has been relieved of his duties, Mercury said.
